insertions.title: Signal logging records data; test points preserve observability
insertions.takeaway: Signal logging selects data for recording and inspection, while a test point deliberately preserves a signal for observability in supported workflows; neither is an SDI marker and neither alone proves a requirement.
insertions.cloneRationale: Slide 6 provides the strongest large-image-plus-stacked-callouts frame in the same section and varies the composition from the immediately preceding slide 7.

asset.source: user image 1 supplied with the v6 request
asset.placement: Replace the slide-6 screenshot in its existing image well; preserve aspect ratio and crop rather than stretch.

contentPlan: SIGNAL LOGGING — records selected signal data for Simulation Data Inspector or programmatic access.
TEST POINT — preserves a signal as an observable point in supported simulation, testing, and code workflows.
RELATIONSHIP — a test point can be logged, but test-point status and logging status are separate properties.
VISIBLE BADGES — model overlays show instrumentation metadata; SDI markers and sample points annotate already logged traces.
USE WITH INTENT — log what an analysis needs and designate test points only when the verification or integration strategy requires them.
notesRequirements: Give the GUI path for enabling logging and for designating or displaying test points in MATLAB R2023b, noting that exact toolstrip grouping can vary by selection.
Explain that logging produces recorded data only when the model runs; a test-point designation by itself does not create an SDI run.
State that the training package currently demonstrates signal logging and SDI artifacts, not a generated-code test-point workflow.
Use official MathWorks signal-logging and test-point documentation in [Sources].

insertions.title: Model Settings control how the model compiles, simulates, and builds
insertions.takeaway: Inspect Model Settings before changing them because solver, timing, data, diagnostics, and code-generation configuration can change behavior and evidence; save only intentional, reviewed edits.
insertions.cloneRationale: Slide 24 has a wide authentic UI image with four concise explanatory cards, ideal for a Model Settings dialog plus check/change/verify/save guidance.

asset.source: user image 2 supplied with the v6 request
asset.placement: Replace the Data Inspector screenshot; keep the screenshot readable and replace all four right-side cards and the bottom caption.

contentPlan: OPEN — Modeling tab > Model Settings, or use the model configuration entry point available in the current editor.
CHECK — solver type, fixed-step size or sample timing, data import/export, diagnostics, and active configuration reference.
CHANGE — edit only the parameter required by the controlled task; note model-reference implications.
VERIFY + SAVE — update the diagram, rerun affected evidence, review diagnostics, and save only under the approved baseline process.
notesRequirements: Include concise MATLAB equivalents such as getActiveConfigSet, get_param, and set_param, but keep commands subordinate to the controlled GUI workflow.
Tie the example to the repository's fixed-step Sample_time = 0.02 s configuration without implying every parameter is safe to change.
Warn that an unsaved Model Settings change can alter results and that changes inherited by referenced models require deliberate review.
Use official MathWorks Model Settings or Configuration Parameters documentation in [Sources].

adjacentNotesContext.followingInsert: Model Advisor evaluates the selected model and configuration, so the component scope and active settings must be understood first.

insertions.title: Model Advisor turns component checks into a reviewable workflow
insertions.takeaway: Choose the intended component and check set, run Model Advisor, review each finding, disposition exceptions, and retain the report; a green dashboard is evidence input rather than automatic compliance.
insertions.cloneRationale: Slide 37 supplies a six-stage horizontal workflow and room for scope, review, and evidence guidance; its dark frame creates visual pacing between the two screenshot slides and the light Polyspace comparison.
contentPlan: SCOPE — open the component or subsystem to be checked.
LAUNCH — open Model Advisor from the Modeling or Apps workflow available in the installed release.
SELECT — choose the project-approved check configuration; do not run an unexplained all-checks set.
RUN — execute checks against the controlled model state and active configuration.
REVIEW — inspect failures, warnings, justifications, and applicability rather than counting only pass icons.
REPORT + DISPOSITION — correct, justify, assign, rerun, and retain the dated report with configuration context.
notesRequirements: Present this as the recommended component-check workflow, not as evidence that Model Advisor was executed for the current package.
State that no retained Model Advisor report was identified in v5 or the current repository evidence set.
Explain that check applicability and acceptable justifications are governed by project plans and model standards.
Use official MathWorks Model Advisor documentation in [Sources].

adjacentNotesContext.precedingInsert: The active configuration and selected component define the check context.
adjacentNotesContext.followingInsert: Polyspace is a future code-analysis workflow, distinct from model checks.

insertions.title: Polyspace separates defect finding from formal proof
insertions.takeaway: Bug Finder targets likely coding defects and security weaknesses, while Code Prover uses formal methods to prove the absence of specified runtime errors; both are future placeholders here and produced no evidence for this package.
insertions.cloneRationale: Slide 4 is the clearest balanced two-column comparison frame and keeps the future-tool distinction readable without fabricating a product screenshot.
contentPlan: POLYSPACE BUG FINDER — static analysis that reports probable defects, coding-rule issues, and selected security weaknesses for review and disposition.
POLYSPACE CODE PROVER — formal analysis that can prove the absence of specified runtime errors under the analyzed assumptions and configuration.
FUTURE PLACEHOLDER — neither product was installed, configured, or executed for the current training baseline.
DEPENDENCY — meaningful code analysis requires appropriate source or generated code, configuration, assumptions, and a controlled review process.
notesRequirements: Keep Bug Finder and Code Prover claims distinct and bounded by the actual analyzed configuration and assumptions.
State explicitly that this repository makes no production-code generation or generated-code verification claim and that Embedded Coder is unavailable in the captured environment.
Do not imply that a clean Polyspace result equals certification approval.
Use official MathWorks Polyspace Bug Finder and Code Prover documentation in [Sources].

adjacentNotesContext.precedingInsert: Model Advisor checks models; Polyspace analyzes code. The slides must not blend those scopes.

insertions.title: Ctrl+D validates model semantics; Ctrl+B invokes a configured build
insertions.takeaway: For PitchRateLimiter_Harness, use Ctrl+D to validate the harness and referenced-component interface before running the MATLAB assessment driver; Ctrl+B is a separate configured code build and is not the harness test command.
insertions.cloneRationale: Slide 25 is a high-contrast two-column comparison that clearly separates two often-confused commands and forms a visual bridge from the light harness slide to the light Data Inspector slide.
contentPlan: CTRL+D — Update Diagram: resolves model references, propagates types, dimensions, sample times, and parameters, and surfaces compile or interface diagnostics.
CTRL+D RESULT — updated compiled semantics and diagnostics; it does not execute the test cases, create an SDI run, or generate production code.
CTRL+B — Build: invokes the model's configured code-generation or build process and depends on products, configuration, toolchain, and target.
CTRL+B RESULT — generated or compiled build artifacts only when a supported build is configured; it is not proof that the harness assessments passed.
HARNESS PATH — update PitchRateLimiter_Harness, then run run_pitch_rate_limiter_tests.m to execute stimuli and evaluate expected results.
notesRequirements: Include MATLAB equivalents: set_param(model,'SimulationCommand','update') for update and slbuild(model) for a configured build, with release and licensing caveats.
Reinforce the v5 slide-23 note: the harness is a standalone Simulink model and its expected values, tolerances, and oracle live in run_pitch_rate_limiter_tests.m.
State that Embedded Coder was unavailable and no production code was generated or verified for this package.
Use official MathWorks model-update and Simulink Coder build documentation in [Sources].

adjacentNotesContext.precedingV5Slide23: Defines the harness, referenced unit under test, deterministic inputs, output capture, and external MATLAB oracle.
adjacentNotesContext.followingV5Slide24: Moves from model preparation and execution distinctions to inspecting a saved run in Data Inspector.

insertions.title: RCF verifies and signs off system requirements independently
insertions.takeaway: The training package can hand off controlled requirements, configuration, traceability, test evidence, and open limitations, but independent RCF system-requirements verification and sign-off remain a future program-controlled activity.
insertions.cloneRationale: Slide 41 already uses an evidence-versus-boundary two-column frame, making it the most direct template for package handoff versus independent RCF responsibility; differentiate the clone with an amber FUTURE gate.
contentPlan: PACKAGE HANDOFF — controlled system and allocated software requirements, model and data baseline identifiers, bidirectional traceability, executed results, limitations, anomalies, and review records.
INDEPENDENT RCF — verify system-requirement correctness and completeness, assess traceability and verification adequacy, resolve or accept open items under approved authority, and record sign-off.
FUTURE PROGRAM PLACEHOLDER — no RCF review, approval, or sign-off artifact is present in the training package.
BOUNDARY — RCF sign-off does not convert classroom examples into an approved aircraft baseline or certification approval.
notesRequirements: Use the acronym RCF exactly as supplied; do not invent or expand its name without a program-controlled definition.
Present responsibilities as a handoff placeholder and defer exact entrance criteria, independence assignments, approvals, and records to the approved program plans.
State that the current repository contains no RCF sign-off evidence and that the slide records a future responsibility, not completed work.

Reference the user-directed RCF role plus applicable approved program plans; FAA or NASA lifecycle sources may provide general assurance context but must not be cited as defining this program-specific acronym.
